content.comment_body: Hi, I'm having trouble with my Ethernet connection—it shows up blank. I've already checked previous threads in this forum and tried everything recommended, but nothing has worked: 1. I ran [product_name] as administrator during installation. 2. I checked my WiFi and network adapters for special characters, updated all network adapters, disabled and enabled the adapters—problem remains. 3. I updated to [product_name] [version_no], but the issue persists. 4. I reinstalled Windows, but the problem is still there. 5. Previously, [product_name] [version_no] worked fine on my old Windows, but after reinstalling Windows due to a crash, this issue started. I'm really frustrated with this. Any advice would be appreciated.
Here's a screenshot of my network adapter.
Could it be that an incorrectly installed PCI Simple Communications Controller is causing the problem?
I've updated it, but the problem still persists.
Inside the folder "C:\[user_name]\.[product_name][version_no]" there's a file named "Application.ini". The "port=" entry shows the name of the Ethernet device.
My Application.ini is different. It says "PORT = com 1". Do you have any suggestions?
Unfortunately, it seems your [product_name] does not have an Ethernet device installed as per your installation setup. If I were in your position, I'd submit a support request.

Hi, I think I've found the cause—it seems the hardware driver is incompatible with [product_name]. I installed [product_name] on another computer and it successfully detected the wireless LAN, but Ethernet highlights are still missing due to the same driver issue on both computers. I'm planning to try a USB-to-Ethernet adapter tonight and hope that resolves it. I've attached the latest screenshot.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faces ongoing Ethernet connection issues with [product_name] ([version_no]), especially after reinstalling Windows. The software isn't detecting the Ethernet device—only a blank window appears. Efforts to update drivers, reinstall the software and Windows, and adjust adapter settings have not helped. Interestingly, installation on another computer identified wireless LAN correctly, suggesting the root cause is hardware driver compatibility for Ethernet interfaces, combined with a lack of detailed diagnostic feedback from the software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects [product_name] to automatically detect available Ethernet devices after installation or a Windows update, with a simple setup and clear network adapter selection options provided by the software.
